# Sample Flat Rubrics

This file shows the supported markdown review surface that the included scripts can normalize or package directly.

## Week 1 Discussion: Introductions and Predictions

- Kind: discussion
- Source Title: Week 1 Discussion: Predictions & Introductions
- Source ID: 266
- Grade Item ID: SAMPLE-899620

| Criterion | Weight | Advanced 100% | Proficient 90% | Developing 75% | Needs Improvement 0% |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Introduction and Prediction Example | 40 | Clearly introduces the learner and provides a specific prediction example that fits the prompt. | Introduces the learner and provides a relevant example with only minor gaps in detail. | Provides a limited introduction or an underdeveloped example. | Does not provide a usable introduction or prediction example. |
| Prediction Reasoning and Stakes | 35 | Clearly explains what informed the prediction, the decision it shaped, and what was at stake. | Explains the prediction logic and stakes with only minor gaps in development. | Partially explains the reasoning or stakes but remains surface-level. | Does not adequately explain the reasoning or stakes. |
| Writing Conventions and Professionalism | 25 | Uses clear, professional writing with strong control and negligible mechanical issues. | Uses generally clear and professional writing with minor issues. | Shows uneven writing control or professionalism. | Writing is unclear or error-heavy enough to interfere with understanding. |

## Project Checkpoint 1: Organization Selection and AI Risk Analysis

- Kind: assignment
- Source Title: Week 2: Initial Project Work
- Source ID: 275
- Grade Item ID: SAMPLE-917685

| Criterion | Weight | Advanced 100% | Proficient 90% | Developing 75% | Needs Improvement 0% |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Organization and Data Environment | 25 | Clearly identifies the organization and accurately describes the main types of data it processes. | Identifies the organization and its data environment with only minor gaps. | Identifies the organization but describes the data environment only partially. | Does not clearly identify the organization or its data environment. |
| Sensitivities, Risks, and Constraints | 25 | Thoughtfully analyzes the likely sensitivities, risks, and relevant constraints. | Analyzes the main risks and constraints with only minor gaps. | Identifies some risks or constraints, but the analysis is general or incomplete. | Does not adequately analyze the relevant sensitivities, risks, or constraints. |
| Responsible AI Implications | 20 | Clearly explains what the identified constraints imply for responsible AI implementation. | Explains the responsible AI implications reasonably well with minor gaps. | Offers a limited or loosely connected discussion of implications. | Does not adequately explain what the constraints imply for responsible AI implementation. |
| Use of Course Evidence | 20 | Uses relevant course resources or case materials to justify the analysis. | Uses course resources appropriately with only minor limits. | Refers to course material in a limited way or relies too heavily on assumptions. | Does not use course resources meaningfully. |
| Writing Conventions and Professionalism | 10 | Uses polished, professional writing conventions appropriate to graduate-level work. | Uses clear and professional writing overall, with minor issues. | Shows uneven control of writing conventions or professional tone. | Writing is unclear, error-heavy, or insufficiently professional for the task. |
